source_review.notes: Checked all eight authoritative records. NASA identifies SP-2016-6105 Rev. 2 as its Systems Engineering Handbook; ISO records ISO/IEC/IEEE 15288:2023 as the current published system-lifecycle standard; NIST records both SP 800-160 volumes and revisions as final; MIT provides the STPA and CAST handbooks; GAO provides the revised 2023 Agile Assessment Guide; the DoD engineering policy page indexes the February 2022 Systems Engineering Guidebook. ISO and GAO may challenge automated retrieval, but current primary records were verified.

evidence: Reviewed the whole-system review vector, necessary readiness implication, evidence envelope, and exercise percentage with balanced GitHub math delimiters.
notation_and_syntax.notes: The eight review dimensions and purpose/configuration/time bounds match their prose definitions and do not imply compensability.

evidence: Recomputed the executable ledger: 3 mission threads times 8 gates gives 24 checks; one failed operations/recovery gate leaves 23 passes and one failure.
Recomputed Exercise 2: 34 of 36 gates is approximately 94.4 percent.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Both computations correctly reject score compensation for a missing decision-critical gate.

evidence: Checked W(q,k,t)=<V,B,R,A,I,H,E,O> against the stakeholder, boundary, requirement, architecture, interface, governance, evidence, and operations definitions.
Checked that eligibility implies all applicable dimensions without claiming evidence truth or sufficiency.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The formalism is a noncompensable completeness screen for review claims, not a proof of system readiness.

evidence: Reviewed nominal, peak, degraded, emergency, maintenance, recovery, transition, adversarial, retirement, mixed-version, supplier-change, jurisdiction-change, and population-expansion cases.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: The review method includes technical, human, organizational, policy, supplier, environmental, and lifecycle boundaries and explicit re-review triggers.

evidence: Checked ten examples and five answers against the invariants for configuration identity, end-to-end threads, hard constraints, evidence applicability, finding closure, residual-risk authority, enforceable conditions, dissent, and bounded approval.
invariant_checking.notes: No example treats team status, document presence, component tests, certification, backup artifacts, action assignment, human signature, or prior approval as whole-system readiness.

proof_review.notes: No theorem that a finite review proves future system success is claimed.

proof_sketch_labeling.notes: The ten-part mechanism section is a decision-review workflow, not a proof sketch.

evidence: The Python fixture identifies itself as declared metadata and explicitly disclaims performing a whole-system review.

Analysis, simulation, test, audit, demonstration, operational, incident, supplier, human, and recovery evidence is bounded by purpose, configuration, thread, population, environment, mode, period, and assumptions.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The chapter treats review as disciplined sampling and judgment and never generalizes a narrow demonstration to universal readiness.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed distinctions among capability, whole-system review, review basis, mission thread, claim, finding, action, closure, residual risk, condition, dissent, decision package, verification, validation, and approval envelope.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed chartering, review competence and independence, configuration freeze, claim maps, mission threads, boundary challenge, requirements and architecture reconciliation, integrated risk, evidence quality, recovery, organizational feasibility, findings, dissent, recommendations, and reconstructable decision records.

pedagogical_review.notes: Reviewed the capstone integration of the full program, executable mission-thread gate, ten distinct review cases, and five exercises progressing from charter design and arithmetic to payment, recovery finding, and platform-transfer reviews.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic, practitioner, regulator, certification, or independent whole-system review is claimed. The chapter cannot authorize a real capability.
